span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Isoflurane reduces cochlear blood flow, blocks acetylcholine receptors and enhances GABA-gated currents, which raises medial olivocochlear efferent inhibition and so depresses auditory sensitivity in the anesthetized state
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Behaviourally relevant high frequencies are over-represented in the mouse auditory cortex because the mouse hearing range extends much further upward, which is why the newly found regions are all high-frequency ones
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Imaging was confined to the right auditory cortex, so lateralization of vocal processing could not be assessed.
span.note: what this limits: any lateralisation claim: A CRANIOTOMY WAS MADE ONLY OVER THE RIGHT AC
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Isoflurane was used as a model of the sleeping brain, and whether the state effects are anaesthetic or sleep-related is unresolved.
span.note: what this limits: the sleep interpretation of the state effects: REPLICATION OF OUR FINDINGS DURING NATURAL SLEEP WILL CLARIFY WHETHER CHANGES IN HEARING SENSITIVITY RESULT FROM USING ISOFLURANE OR ARE ASSOCIATED WITH SLEEP PROCESSES
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The comparison of natural sleep against awake and anaesthetized states is left to future work.
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 1: THE IMPACT OF SLEEP COMPARED TO ANESTHETIZED AND AWAKE STATES SHOULD BE STUDIED IN THE FUTURE
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The map of this cortex has been revised repeatedly, and the paper attributes the revisions to advances in technique rather than to new anatomy.
span.note: what this limits: any area label in the mouse auditory cortex literature: the paper states the tonotopic organisation of the belt area has been significantly updated as neuroimaging and recording advanced
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: An area in the classical map is reported as dissolvable into parts of two others, on the evidence of one technique.
span.note: what this limits: the UF area as a unit in the mouse auditory map: electrophysiological measurements are reported as suggesting it should be considered subparts of AAF and AI
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The tonotopic map rests on a per-frequency threshold identified by the experimenters.
span.note: what this limits: the tonotopic maps in this paper: for each frequency a threshold level was identified and used to determine the map
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The paper's own account of why the map keeps changing is an account of instruments, not of findings - decades of technological advancement producing significant updates to the organisation. On that account the current map is the current technique's map, and the paper is adding a fourth.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: a deliberately LARGE craniotomy, 3 to 4 mm across, over the auditory cortical regions
span.note: eliminates: that the map is shaped by the size of the recording window rather than by the cortex - a small window would truncate the functional organisation being measured
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: responsive pixels were identified first and used to exclude the unresponsive ones from analysis
span.note: eliminates: that unresponsive pixels dilute the signal and flatten the functional map
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: UF —part-of→ AI
span.note: differs in: WHICH TECHNIQUE IS ASKED. 'ELECTROPHYSIOLOGICAL MEASUREMENTS suggest the UF area should be considered as SUBPARTS of the AAF and AI' - so on that instrument UF is not an area at all but pieces of two others. The record already carries THREE readings of AI as senses, one per technique: optical calcium imaging splits it into two high-frequency regions, flavoprotein autofluorescence makes the dorsal part discrete, widefield imaging introduces a new layout entirely · strength of the relation: 0.7 — AN AREA THAT DISSOLVES INTO PARTS OF TWO OTHERS DEPENDING ON THE METHOD. The boundary is not a fact the techniques disagree about - each technique constitutes a different partition, and all of them are current.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Three previously uncharacterised tonotopic regions of mouse auditory cortex - the dorsal anterior field, the posterior auditory field and the ventral posterior auditory field - were identified, all preferentially responsive to high frequencies and lying dorsal and caudal to the known areas.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Tonotopic maps were stable within a single 25-minute session, across three consecutive weeks in the same mouse, and across the twelve animals.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: High-frequency responses in AI-H and UF were larger in awake than in isoflurane-anesthetized mice, implying reduced high-frequency hearing sensitivity under anesthesia.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Under anesthesia the cortical area encoding slow FM sweep rates expanded and the area encoding fast sweep rates shrank across AAF, DA and UF.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Contrary to an earlier report of no difference, upward and downward FM sweep maps do differ: the slow-rate centre in AI sits about 350 micrometres more rostral for downward sweeps.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Ultrasonic vocalizations drove stronger responses than pure tones specifically in the regions tuned to fast FM sweep rates (AII, DP, PAF, VPAF and a zone between UF and AAF), and not in the high-frequency tonotopic regions.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Best frequency changes with distance along a tonotopic gradient as a sigmoid: middle frequencies change steeply over a short stretch of cortex while low and high frequencies occupy longer stretches.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Tone-evoked cortical activity stays near its source, so tonotopic maps computed from any averaging window between 100 ms and 1000 ms after onset come out identical.
span.note: retracted: RE-GROUNDED - THE POINTER WAS WRONG, NOT THE CLAIM. The old evidence was verbatim, anchored and correctly cut, and it contained NONE of this claim's numbers (100, 1000). The paper states the claim in one sentence elsewhere and the tagger did not use it. CLAUDE_B, 2026-08-23: `WE HAVE SPENT THE DAY VERIFYING THAT QUOTES ARE REAL AND NONE OF IT ASKS WHETHER THEY ARE RELEVANT.` Confirmed by reading the claim, the old span and the candidate together; the candidate carries every number AND the claim's own content words.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The tonotopic map spans 2 mm rostro-caudally and 1.9 mm dorso-ventrally, so the conventional 2x2 mm imaging window used in earlier work is too small to capture all of it.
